name: Tonga
summary: A red field with a white canton bearing a red cross. Adopted in 1875 under King George Tupou I, its design is protected by the constitution, which says it may never be changed.
origin: King George Tupou I, who converted to Christianity and unified Tonga, wanted a flag expressing the Christian faith. An earlier version resembled the Red Cross flag, so a red field was added. The 1875 Constitution established it and forbids altering it.

colors.name: Red
colors.meaning: The blood of Christ shed on the cross.

symbols.name: Red cross
symbols.description: A red cross in the white canton.
symbols.meaning: Christianity, the faith of the nation.

facts: Article 47 of the Constitution states the flag shall never be altered.
Tonga was never formally colonised, though it was a British protected state from 1900 to 1970.
It is one of the few flags with a cross in the canton, along with Greece's.
clues: Red with a white canton holding a red cross.
Its constitution says it may never be changed.
Its king chose it to express his Christian faith in 1875.
